title: Graph Algorithms Explorer
description: Run community detection and link prediction on an 18-node network and interpret both results.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Knowledge Graph Applications and Data Architecture
chapter_title: Knowledge Graph Applications and Data Architecture

educational.learningObjective: Given a sample network, the learner will apply community detection to identify densely connected clusters and apply link prediction to identify a plausible missing edge, then interpret both results.
prerequisites: Knows what a node, an edge and a degree are
learningOutcomes: Apply community detection and interpret the resulting clusters
Apply link prediction and interpret the score
Explain why a predicted link is a hypothesis rather than a fact
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Ask learners to name the bridging nodes and to explain what removing one of them would do to the network's structure.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Algorithm-on-demand over a fixed network with per-node inspection
pedagogical.feedbackType: Recoloring, a dashed predicted edge with its score, and a generated interpretation
misconceptionsAddressed: That community detection needs the groups to be labeled in advance
That a high-scoring predicted link is a discovered fact
discussionQuestions: Why does label propagation find the same communities a human would?
What is the difference between a prediction being likely and being true?
Where would acting on link prediction be helpful, and where would it be intrusive?
